title: Exactness of colimits and amenability are independent for categories of finite substructures
subject: math.CT
abstract: Let M be a countable homogeneous structure, G its automorphism group and A the category of its finite substructures and embeddings. The colimit functor on diagrams of R-modules indexed by A is exact if and only if the functor of coinvariants N ↦ N_G is exact on the R[G]-modules in which every element has an open stabilizer; this is a property of the topos of continuous G-sets. We compare it with amenability of G, the existence of invariant probability measures on compact spaces on which G acts, and show that neither implies the other. For the generic partially ordered set with an independent linear order, colimits are exact over every ring, while the group is not amenable by a result of Kechris and Sokić. For the vector space of countable dimension over the field with two elements, with a generic linear order on its non-zero vectors, the group is amenable and colimits are exact over the rational numbers, but they are exact over no ring in which 2 is not invertible. The first statement rests on a transfer theorem: if a subgroup H has exact coinvariants and finitely many orbits on each G/G_B, then exactness for G over a field k is equivalent to the existence of a G-invariant, finitely additive, k-valued function of total mass 1 on the expansions that H defines; positivity is not required. For posets this function has integer values, given by Euler characteristics of cells of order cones, which are values of the measure of Harman and Snowden for the automorphism group of the ordered real line. A consequence is that the separation property proved by Evans for Ramsey structures holds for a structure that is not a Ramsey structure but is obtained from one by forgetting a relation.
comments:
This paper compares two properties of the automorphism group G of a countable homogeneous structure M: exactness of colimits over the category of finite substructures of M and embeddings, and amenability. Theorem 1.2: colimits of R-modules over this category are exact if and only if coinvariants preserve monomorphisms of smooth R[G]-modules, a property of the topos of continuous G-sets. Theorem 1.3 (transfer): given a subgroup H with exact coinvariants and finitely many orbits on each G/G_B, exactness over a field k is equivalent to a G-invariant, finitely additive, k-valued function of total mass 1 on the expansions that H defines. Theorem 1.4: for the generic poset with an independent linear order, colimits are exact over every ring, while G is not amenable (Kechris-Sokić). Theorem 1.5: for the ordered F_2-vector space of countable dimension, G is amenable and colimits are exact over every Q-algebra, but over no ring in which 2 is not invertible. Corollary 1.6: Evans's membership test and separation property hold for the generic poset with an independent linear order.

How it was produced. The mathematics comes from a research run of GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, that ended on 18 November 2026 (run FREX), in answer to a research prompt of this project that followed up the question of the paper Exact, total and filtered small categories (hexagon:2611.01026); the run built on earlier runs of the same model, from one of which the first half of Lemma 3.2 comes. The run gave the statements and proofs of Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 (part (c) over F_2 and Z), of the first sentence of Theorem 1.2, of Theorem 1.3 in the form of a closed co-precompact subgroup, of Lemmas 3.4, 4.1 and 5.1 and of the three steps of Section 5. Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote this text on 25 November 2026 in the setting of that paper and derived every proof again; its own are the direct proof of Proposition 2.4 (the run cites Isbell and Mitchell), the formulation of Theorem 1.3 by finite sets of double cosets, the second sentence of Theorem 1.2 and Remark 2.1 (after a remark by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max in the project's notes), Theorem 1.5 (c) over every ring in which 2 is not invertible, Lemma 2.2, Corollary 1.6 and Remarks 3.6, 4.2 and 4.3.

How it was checked. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max followed the run's text step by step at its intake (19 and 24 November 2026). The writer ran a program in exact integer arithmetic that confirms Lemma 4.1 for all 4474 partial orders on at most five labelled points, the example of Remark 4.2 and the two identities of the proof of Theorem 1.5 (c) for all injective linear maps into F_2^n, n <= 5. Another Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, in a separate run, checked the finished text independently on 25 November 2026: before reading the proofs it proved Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Proposition 2.4, Theorem 1.5 (c) and the non-amenability in Theorem 1.4 itself, the last two by other routes (the non-amenability by a direct argument that does not use the ordering property, confirmed by a linear program on structures with at most four points); it then followed every proof, checked Lemma 4.1 by another method, opened every citation but Hodges's book at the places cited, ran both programs, found no theorem wrong and proposed seven repairs, among them the converse in Remark 4.3 (the earlier sentence was false as written) and the last step of Theorem 1.3 (c), which the writer applied. Before posting, the main session, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, read every page of the repaired text, checked the example of the translations of Z added after the check and the checker's proof of non-amenability, and corrected the credit for Theorem 1.5 (c).
